findings.title: Stale replica read makes cleanup de-index a live entry permanently
findings.why_it_matters: On a redis_cluster2 store configured to read from replicas (routeByLatency = true, or useReadOnly = true), a file that was just written can vanish from directory listings for good. The listing's GET is served by a replica that has not yet received the value, the new cleanup then issues ZREM against the master, and the 'is the value back?' recheck (EXISTS) is another read-only command routed to the same lagging replica, so it also says 'absent' and the member is not restored. Before this change the same stale read only skipped the entry for that one listing; now the index member is gone until something calls InsertEntry on that path again (UpdateEntry never re-adds it), which breaks the stated guarantee that the repair never hides a live entry. The absence decision has to be made against the master, or the cleanup has to be disabled when reads may be stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the absence decision master-authoritative before removing anything. Smallest change: have RedisCluster2Store.initialize record `store.replicaReads = readOnly || routeByLatency` on UniversalRedis2Store and have ListDirectoryEntries skip removeOrphanedDirectoryListMember when it is set (restores the pre-change transient-skip behavior in that mode only). Alternative that keeps cleanup working in that mode: issue the EXISTS on the value key through store.Client.TxPipelined, which go-redis always routes to the slot master (osscluster.go:1881 `node, err := state.slotMasterNode(slot)`), do it once before the ZREM (return without removing if the value exists) and again for the post-ZREM recheck. Assumption: a master round trip per orphan is acceptable because each orphan is only cleaned once.
evidence: weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:238 -- if err := store.Client.ZRem(ctx, dirListKey, fileName).Err(); err != nil {   /   weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:245 -- exists, err := store.Client.Exists(ctx, store.getKey(string(path))).Result()

weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:99-101 -- FindEntry: `data, err := store.Client.Get(...)`; `if err == redis.Nil { return nil, filer_pb.ErrNotFound }` -- a GET answered by a replica that lacks the key is indistinguishable from a deleted/expired value, so the `err == filer_pb.ErrNotFound` guard at :207 does not filter it out.

weed/filer/redis2/redis_cluster_store.go:53-54 -- `ReadOnly: readOnly, RouteByLatency: routeByLatency,` passed to redis.ClusterOptions from the `useReadOnly` / `routeByLatency` config keys (:40-41). weed/command/scaffold/filer.toml:290 documents `routeByLatency` for [redis_cluster2] ('automatically use the closest Redis server for reads').

go-redis v9.21.0 osscluster.go:205-206 -- `if opt.RouteByLatency || opt.RouteRandomly { opt.ReadOnly = true }`; osscluster.go:2399-2405 cmdNode -- `if c.opt.ReadOnly { cmdInfo := c.cmdInfo(ctx, cmdName); if cmdInfo != nil && cmdInfo.ReadOnly { return c.slotReadOnlyNode(state, slot) } } return state.slotMasterNode(slot)`. GET, EXISTS and ZRANGEBYLEX are read-only commands and go to slotReadOnlyNode; ZREM/ZADD go to the master.

go-redis v9.21.0 osscluster.go:935-946 slotSlaveNode -- with one replica per shard (`case 2`) it always returns the replica unless it is Failing()/Loading(); a replica that is merely behind is neither, so GET and the follow-up EXISTS hit the same lagging node. With routeByLatency, slotClosestNode (:963) returns whichever node has the lowest latency, which is a replica whenever the filer sits closer to it than to the master.

Scenario: (1) InsertEntry /d/f: SET value on the master of the value's slot, then ZADD NX member on the master of the `/d\x00` slot (universal_redis_store.go:58-68). (2) A listing of /d (e.g. S3 LIST right after PUT) reads ZRANGEBYLEX from a replica that already has the member. (3) GET /d/f is routed to a replica of the value's shard that is behind (async replication lag, replica link down or mid-resync while still serving stale data) -> redis.Nil -> ErrNotFound. (4) removeOrphanedDirectoryListMember: ZREM goes to the master and removes the member of a live entry. (5) EXISTS goes to the same lagging replica -> 0 -> return without ZAddNX. (6) The value is live on the master but has no index member; UpdateEntry is `return store.doInsertEntry(ctx, entry)` (:94) and never re-adds it. Value key and index key are in different slots, so the two reads are served by independently lagging replicas; even within one shard with several replicas the two reads can land on different replicas.

Commit 6c8fde664's own guard is defeated by the same routing: its recheck is the only thing protecting a concurrent InsertEntry, and under replica reads that recheck does not observe the SET that just landed on the master.

Reachability note: the scaffold documents the key as `readOnly` (filer.toml:288) while the code reads `useReadOnly`, so the documented `readOnly = true` is a no-op; the reachable switches are the documented `routeByLatency = true` and the undocumented `useReadOnly` key. Both default to false, so default deployments and the single-node redis2 / redis2_sentinel stores (master-only reads) are not affected.

residual_risks: Partial failure inside removeOrphanedDirectoryListMember is silent and unrecoverable: if ZREM succeeds and the final ZAddNX (universal_redis_store.go:250, result discarded) fails or is skipped because the request context ended, a value recreated by a concurrent InsertEntry is left with no index member and nothing logs or retries it. Needs a concurrent insert plus an error at that exact command, so the window is narrow; not verified how go-redis treats a cancelled ctx between the three commands.

UpdateEntry is `doInsertEntry` only and never adds the index member (universal_redis_store.go:92-95). Before this change a lingering member made a value rewritten by UpdateEntry visible again; now an UpdateEntry that lands after a listing cleaned the member (value expired/evicted between the caller's read and its write-back, e.g. the store-level write-back at weed/server/filer_grpc_server_remote.go:312 after a remote-object download) leaves a value that is findable by path but absent from listings. Callers inspected re-read the entry shortly before updating, so the window is small.

The adjacent logical-expiry branch (universal_redis_store.go:215-218) still does an unconditional DEL + ZREM with no recheck, i.e. the same interleaving commit 6c8fde664 closes for the not-found branch remains open there and can additionally delete a freshly re-inserted value. Pre-existing and untouched by this diff.
Replica-read analysis rests on Redis reporting GET/EXISTS/ZRANGEBYLEX as read-only in COMMAND metadata (go-redis takes the flag from the server); no live cluster was available to observe the routing.
testing_gaps: The three new tests never run in CI: newTestStore skips unless RUN_REDIS_TESTS=1, and nothing in the repository sets it (no file under .github/ or docker/compose mentions redis). A regression in the ZREM / re-add logic stays green; the suite only has value when someone runs it by hand against a local redis-server.
All tests use a single-node redis.NewClient, so the cluster client and replica-read routing (useReadOnly / routeByLatency) that RedisCluster2Store exposes are never exercised against the new cleanup.

No test interleaves an InsertEntry between the listing's FindEntry and the helper's ZREM/EXISTS. TestRemoveOrphanedDirectoryListMemberKeepsRecreatedEntry only calls the helper with the value already present, which covers the re-add but not the ordering the second commit is about (e.g. SET landing after EXISTS, or a DeleteEntry landing between EXISTS and ZAddNX).
